Prickly pears can generate solar electricity

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (591 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, most plants rely on real-time photosynthesis for food, which means they aren’t generating energy unless the sun is out.
  • Sources indicate that plants generally absorb carbon dioxide through pores in their leaves, but the prickly pear can’t afford such an evolutionary luxury.
  • It has been revealed that environmental biologists certainly did.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, most plants rely on real-time photosynthesis for food, which means they aren’t generating energy unless the sun is out. Meanwhile, cacti like the prickly pear must get creative in order to survive the harsh conditions they live in. With high temperatures and little water, these plants and similar species like aloe and pineapple evolved a specialized process called crassulacean acid metabolism (CAM). The overall principles are the same, but instead of converting carbon dioxide (CO₂) and water into sugars solely during daylight, CAM allows a prickly pear to extend its photosynthesis over a full 24 hours.

Sources indicate that plants generally absorb carbon dioxide through pores in their leaves, but the prickly pear can’t afford such an evolutionary luxury. The desert heat would turn those same tiny openings into water drains. With CAM, a prickly pear only absorbs carbon dioxide at night, and subsequently turns it into malic acid. Photosynthesis later breaks down the acid—but only on the side of the plant directly exposed to sunlight. The shady side retains its malic acid, creating a pH concentration gradient. Interestingly, this pH imbalance is also one of the underlying principles for generating electricity…see where this is going?

It has been revealed that environmental biologists certainly did. In a study published today in the journal Plants, People, Planet, a team at the University of California, Santa Cruz, (UC Santa Cruz) detailed a upcoming, interdisciplinary system that transforms the common prickly pear into a green solar panel. Although prickly pear voltages aren’t enough to deliver a noticeable jolt, they are strong enough to power the tiny sensors often used by farmers to monitor their crops. With some additional fine-tuning, their novel methods could offer a promising, sustainable adaptation to ongoing climate concerns.

Industry observers note that “It was just so nice to have 10 students in a room from all across campus working together on a single project. When we’re looking at climate solutions, that’s what we need,” Charlie Chesney, a UC Santa Cruz environmental scientist and study co-author, mentioned in a statement.

In a recent development, wiring a single spiky plant doesn’t do much, but linking them together adds up. As few as eight prickly pears are enough to generate 4.5 volts of electricity—nearly three times the charge of a commercial AA battery. That’s more than enough to power the common, low-energy sensors used to assess plants.

“There are many commercial applications of cacti [for] monitoring their health using a low-power system like ours, that is just operating off on the side and is self-powered,” explained UC Santa Cruz ecologist and study co-author Michael Loik.

He offered one such scenario, where wired prickly pears function as organic “sentinels” that monitor field conditions and relay the information back to a farmer’s office.

“This could be a really interesting avenue to pursue,” he added.

Sources indicate that the idea isn’t limited to the prickly pear, either. Any plant that uses CAM—aloe, pineapple, agave—could benefit from a similar battery upgrade. The team even assessed how the cacti performed under a standard desert challenge like drought. Even after 15 months without water, sample prickly pears weren’t simply surviving—they were still photosynthesizing. In some cases, the resultant voltages were higher than watered control plants.

“This was a really surprising result, but also indicated how resilient a cactus is—it could still produce electricity even when it seems, to us, like it’s near death,” added Chesney.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As no-drip, low-noise job sites become more the global rule rather than the exception, Volvo’s incredibly versatile EWR150 Electric wheeled excavators are proving to be a smart addition to construction and municipal fleets – that’s proving true in Luxembourg, as well.

It has been revealed that the Volvo EWR150 Electric wheeled excavator is helping the postage stamp nation of Luxembourg connect natural freshwater springs to a planned water reservoir, but the work has to be done in an existing groundwater protection zone, where even the smallest fuel spills or oil leaks could have serious consequences. An ideal opportunity, in other words, for a battery electric machine like the EWR150 Electric to shine.

It has been revealed that “Sometimes I miss the sound of the engine,” indicates Thomas Weber, an operator on the project who’d previously worked with the conventional EWR150 wheeled excavator. “But the quieter operation of the EWR150 Electric is more beneficial for me, personally. Compared to the diesel equivalent, I find the performance and power to be identical.”.

Volvo CE took to LinkedIn to share the work being done by the Luxemburgers at construction firm Elenz, touting the Volvo’s clean, quiet running in this highly environment.

For their part, Elenz executives are equally excited about the latest machine. “Going electric is not a regulation, but a requirement for this particular job,” explains Christoph Schommer, Managing Director of Elenz. “We are thoroughly impressed by the EWR150 Electric. Its low noise level is a major advantage here. At the same time, the machine offers plenty of power and consistently delivers the same level of energy.”.

The EWR150 Electric is built around a 270 kWh, 600V li-ion battery pack powering an electric drive motor that’s backed by a KERS-style hydraulic boom energy-recovery system that works like regenerative braking to extend the machine’s operating time. A 0.67 m³ (~0.9 yd³) bucket with 108.5-kN (~ 24,390 lb.) breakout force is standard, and offers a, 8.95 meter (~29 foot) maximum digging reach and 5.23 meter (~17 foot) digging depth. Volvo notes the machine can typically operate for 8–10 hours depending on the application.

In a recent development, elenz is charging their EWR150 Electric overnight using a 32A L2 connection at a nearby sewage treatment plant, which also serves as the project office and a secure parking location for site equipment. By charging overnight, when Elenz’ crew isn’t working, the organization has been able to integrate the massive BEV without changing their existing work schedules.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that it’s been two years since Lego and Formula 1 first partnered up to translate the excitement of the grand prix grid into tiny, plastic, painful-to-step-on brick form. But while the race cars were a realistic low-polygon tribute to the life-size real things, the minifigures that accompanied them were fairly generic. Until now, that is, because the upcoming Lego Speed Champions lineup features all 11 teams on the 2026 grid and all 22 full-time drivers, rendered with realistic driving suits and customized hair.

In a recent development, announced at the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix against a backdrop of several giant minifigures and a full complement of Lego-clad go-karts (now updated with neon LED light strips for the full Vegas experience), this next batch of Speed Champions sets will go on sale March 1, 2027. That makes for plenty of time to build all 11 before the first race of the season in Bahrain, although it’s also yet another thing to wait for during the off-season.

Arvid Lindblad, driver for the Visa Cash App Racing Bulls Team, made at appearance at Lego’s press announcement, and posed with both his large and small Lego likenesses. Asked about his thoughts on the result, the British driver said: “Awesome, nailed it. They got the hair perfect,” adding that, “I’ve always loved Legos, though I never imagined having my own minifigure.”.

It has been revealed that and speaking of hair, yes, the Valteri Bottas minifigure is rocking a mullet. Each plastic hairpiece was approved by the respective drivers. “When we pitched the the hairstyles to the teams and the drivers, they absolutely loved it,” noted Will Thorogood, the Lego designer who led this effort. “They all thought it was as funny as we did.”.

It has been revealed that another key part of bringing out the driver’s personality is the helmets, which are “far more detailed than any helmet we've ever done before with the with the Lego production,” according to Thorogood. Lando Norris’s helmet, for example, “has all the blob details on it” as well as a minifigure Easter egg hidden in the design. Each driver also comes with two facial expressions on opposite sides of the minfigure head; Charles Leclerc’s visage is either relaxed in sunglasses or a more serious grimace, both with the Ferrari driver’s stubbled mustache and goatee.

The cars themselves reflect the new regulations and, indicates Thorogood, “as you look closely, you'll see every single one is built completely differently to capture all the aero details and principles that each of the teams has employed.” These too feature several Easter eggs for Lego fans, such as suspension wishbones made from wizard wands and rear diffuser strakes made from minifigure meat cleavers.

Measuring 7.5 inches long and 2.5 inches wide, the Speed Champions sets will be priced at $29.99 when they go on sale next year. More photos and details are viewable now on the Speed Champions section of the Lego Website.

#17708. Newly introduced Guidelines Recommend Routine Prostate Cancer Screening for Men Over 50

Newly introduced Guidelines Recommend Routine Prostate Cancer Screening for Men Over 50

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1000 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As rates of advanced prostate cancer continue to rise, the American Cancer Society (ACS) has issued latest guidelines recommending routine prostate cancer screening for many men starting at age 50.
  • The updated recommendations, published November 12 in CA: A Cancer Journal for Clinicians, mark a shift from the organization’s previous emphasis on shared decision making about whether to undergo screening.
  • Under the newly introduced guidelines, the ACS recommends regular prostate-specific antigen (PSA) testing beginning at age 50 for men at average risk of prostate cancer and age 45 for those at higher risk.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As rates of advanced prostate cancer continue to rise, the American Cancer Society (ACS) has issued latest guidelines recommending routine prostate cancer screening for many men starting at age 50.

The updated recommendations, published November 12 in CA: A Cancer Journal for Clinicians, mark a shift from the organization’s previous emphasis on shared decision making about whether to undergo screening.

Under the newly introduced guidelines, the ACS recommends regular prostate-specific antigen (PSA) testing beginning at age 50 for men at average risk of prostate cancer and age 45 for those at higher risk.

Advances in MRI technology and biomarker testing may also help doctors determine which men need further testing, potentially reducing unnecessary biopsies and overtreatment.

The ACS last updated its prostate cancer screening guidelines in 2010, when conflicting research findings raised questions about whether the benefits of PSA screening outweighed the potential harms.

At the time, the organization emphasized informed, shared decision making between patients and healthcare professionals.

However, longer-term follow-up studies have since provided stronger evidence of the benefits of early detection, prompting the ACS to conduct a systematic review and upgrade its recommendations.

The authors of the report noted, “In making these recommendations, we recognize that PSA testing is only the first step in a screening cascade that includes secondary testing of men with an elevated PSA level and treatment decisions for men diagnosed with prostate cancer.”.

The fresh guidelines recommend a PSA test every 2 years for men ages 50–69 with an average risk of prostate cancer.

The recommendation for those at high risk is a PSA test every year starting at age 45.

Industry observers note that for men ages 70–74, the ACS recommends individualized decision making. If an individual chooses to be screened, the ACS recommends a PSA test every 2 years until the age of 74.

Ramkishen Narayanan, MD, Director of the Center for Urologic Health at The Roy and Patricia Disney Family Cancer Center at Providence Saint Joseph Medical Center in Burbank, CA, who wasn’t involved in the report, told Healthline that screening shouldn’t automatically be ruled out for men over 75.

“[A] point worth noting is that for men over 75, their PSA history as well as their individual clinical scenarios should be evaluated, and that PSA should not be discouraged in this group of men if their life expectancy and clinical history warrant a PSA check.”.

According to the ACS, approximately 1 in 8 men will be diagnosed with prostate cancer during their lifetime.

Individual risk depends on age, race/ethnicity, and other factors:.

Prostate cancer diagnoses in the United States increased by around 3% per year between 2014 and 2022, according to the ACS.

The rise in diagnoses, particularly advanced-stage prostate cancer, has renewed attention on the importance of regular screening.

“[The] current state of prostate cancer screening guidelines is vague and generalized. This has led to ambiguity, disagreement, and variation of opinion among healthcare providers and institutions in their approach to men’s health,” said S. Adam Ramin, MD, board certified urologist, urologic oncologist, and medical director of Urology Cancer Specialists in Los Angeles, CA, who wasn’t involved in the report.

The updated ACS guidelines drew partly on findings from a 2025 follow-up of the European Randomized Study of Screening for Prostate Cancer (ERSPC), which found that regular PSA screening was associated with a 13% reduction in prostate cancer deaths over 23 years.

A 12-year ERSPC follow-up in 2012 also suggested that regular screening was associated with a decrease in metastatic prostate cancer diagnosis, which is another finding that influenced the updated guidance.

“Prostate cancer can take many years, even decades, to become clinically significant, so it takes a long time for us to see the consequences of changes in screening practices,” Taylor Goodstein, MD, assistant professor of urology in the College of Medicine at the University of Cincinnati, who wasn’t involved in the report, told Healthline.

“With longer follow-up from randomized trials, we now have more convincing evidence that PSA screening reduces the risk of dying from prostate cancer,” she noted.

“The ACS guidelines are vital now because they drive home the most important point that prostate cancer screening saves lives,” said Narayanan.

Healthcare professionals use PSA levels to help determine whether additional testing for prostate cancer may be necessary.

The ACS recommends further testing for men under 70 with PSA levels of 3 ng/mL or higher.

For those ages 70 and older, the ACS recommends further testing if their PSA is 6.5 ng/mL or higher. This is because PSA levels tend to be naturally higher in older men.

You can speak with your healthcare professional to find out more about PSA cutoff levels.

Goodstein told Healthline that the ways this new guidance can change the outlook for prostate cancer are simple.

“If we screen men, we can catch troublesome cancers early, before they have a chance to spread,” she remarked.

According to recent reports, goodstein also emphasized how much the evaluation process has changed. In the past, an elevated PSA level often led directly to a biopsy.

Industry observers note that today, doctors generally repeat the PSA test within two weeks to three months to confirm the result. If PSA levels remain elevated, additional testing, including a prostate MRI or validated biomarker test, can help determine whether a biopsy is necessary.

Narayanan told Healthline, “The new guidelines will hopefully remove any confusion about the value of PSA screening and encourage prostate cancer screening as an integral part of a man’s ‘checkup’.”.

He added that it is worth noting that the DRE (digital rectal exam) adds little value to the initial prostate cancer screening and is no longer something that men should fear.

According to recent reports, “Adoption of this set of specific guidelines standardizes the approach to screening for prostate cancer. It provides a unified effort among all levels of healthcare. It most likely will increase the chances of finding prostate cancer in earlier stages and lead to improved cancer treatment outcomes,” remarked Ramin.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Tesla Charging revealed the newly introduced station on X on Tuesday night with its usual one-liner and a photo of the stalls at sunset:.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that tesla has opened its first Semi Megacharger in Texas, an 8-stall station in Mesquite on the east side of Dallas. With it, Tesla’s map now lists 7 public Megacharger sites and 44 stalls for its electric truck.

Sources indicate that that’s progress. But with six weeks left in 2026, it’s less than a fifth of the 37 sites Tesla planned to have open this year.

Tesla Charging revealed the newly introduced station on X on Tuesday night with its usual one-liner and a photo of the stalls at sunset:.

Latest Tesla Megacharger: Mesquite, TX (8 stalls) https://t.co/UsCFMyCjo7 pic.twitter.com/W4G1e2BHkb.

Tesla’s map lists the site at 2175 S Town East Blvd in Mesquite, with eight Megachargers rated at up to 1.2 MW each.

Texas is where Tesla has the most riding on this network. When Tesla added 64 Megacharger locations to its map in February, Texas got 19 of the 66 planned sites, more than any other state. Mesquite is the first of them to go live, and several other Dallas–Fort Worth sites are still marked “coming soon.”.

Sources indicate that the Pilot truck stop rollout hasn’t reached Texas either. When Pilot opened its first Megacharger in Georgia in October, it named a Flying J in Fort Stockton, Texas, as one of the next sites. It’s still not live on Tesla’s map.

Recent findings suggest that tesla also isn’t alone in DFW. Greenlane, the truck charging joint venture between Daimler Truck, NextEra and BlackRock, confirmed high-power sites in Dallas and Houston in May, open to any electric truck with CCS and MCS connectors. Tesla now has a station operating in the metro.

Here’s every public Megacharger currently live on Tesla’s map:.

Industry observers note that that’s 7 sites and 44 stalls in four states. When we counted in early October, there were four customer-facing sites with 26 stalls. Tulare opened the same week, Hodgkins came on November 10, and now Mesquite.

So Tesla is adding a site roughly every two weeks.

In a recent development, tesla also runs private Megachargers for its own fleet at Giga Nevada and in Carson, California, and it sells Megachargers to fleets and depot operators through its business program. Forum Mobility switched on two at the Port of Long Beach earlier this month. None of those count toward the public network that Semi buyers without their own depot rely on.

In a recent development, tesla’s Q4 2025 shareholder report indicated about 37 Megacharger sites for 2026. Semi program lead Dan Priestley has noted Tesla wants 46 by early 2027.

To me this seems like good progress, sure it's not right on time with their ambitious goal, but they are executing on their charging network and I'm sure more sites will keep opening.

To hit 37, Tesla would need to open 30 more sites in the next 43 days. At the current pace, it ends the year with around 10.

Sources indicate that pilot mentioned in October that nine more of its sites were under construction, so a late burst is possible. But it would have to be a very significant one.

And the trucks are starting to show up. Tesla launched volume production of the Semi in September at a Nevada factory it states can build 50,000 trucks a year, and it remarked last week that Chicago’s first 50 Semis are en route for delivery, a day after Hodgkins opened. Substantial fleets like that customer are installing their own depot chargers anyway, and most Semi charging will happen there. The public network is what lets a Semi leave its home region.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Battlefield Studios is seemingly trying something different with Battlefield 6’s next patch, which everyone assumed would be a standard, mid-season update not intended to change the game significantly.
  • However, it appears that it may bring more to the game than we realised, enough that the developer sees it as an excuse to bring back the pre-launch Battlefield Labs testing initiative.
  • It has been revealed that the December 9 patch kicks off the final phase of the game’s first season, which is set to take the game through the holidays and into the latest year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Battlefield Studios is seemingly trying something different with Battlefield 6’s next patch, which everyone assumed would be a standard, mid-season update not intended to change the game significantly.

However, it appears that it may bring more to the game than we realised, enough that the developer sees it as an excuse to bring back the pre-launch Battlefield Labs testing initiative.

It has been revealed that the December 9 patch kicks off the final phase of the game’s first season, which is set to take the game through the holidays and into the latest year. We’ve known about its content for a while, and it’s definitely the lightest, compared to the two previous phases.

Industry observers note that battlefield Studios announced a host of latest changes that will be included in the same patch, which are apparently significant enough to require player testing. The developer is reviving Battlefield Labs to help it do so, but only for three two-hour sessions, split across the game’s three main server regions (EU, NA, APAC).

All tests are scheduled for today, December 2, and they remain under NDA. Battlefield Labs is also sticking with PC as its chosen platform yet again, though you will be able to join through Steam this time, alongside the EA app.

The focus of the test will be on three key areas that the December 9 patch will be touching. First, there’s footstep audio, an glitch that was really brought into focus with the launch of Redsec Battle Royale. You can expect to hear enemy footsteps from farther away, and intuitively know the type of surface they’re moving on.

According to recent reports, the patch also brings another pass to hit registration and netcode, which BF Studios states should improve responsiveness in close-quarter situations. Finally, there are broader changes to other combat areas that the announcement didn’t elaborate on.

All testing will take place on Eastwood, and Operation Firestorm, rotating between Conquest, and Escalation.

In a recent development, going forward, Battlefield Studios noted to expect Labs to be open to more players, and for the process itself to be smoother. The developer wants to have faster turnaround times, after all, so that the initiative can test smaller changes and be more responsive to player feedback.

Some of the more involved, future sessions will include experiments with map layout changes and various other non-standard compositions of player and vehicle numbers. Of course, you can also expect new maps and modes to be tested in Labs, similar to how the CTE was used in Battlefield 4’s long life.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that when this GM EV1 project car finally drove into daylight, it was 30 years to the day from when the very first EV1 rolled off the assembly line. Nicknamed V212, after a part of its VIN that proves it's the 212th EV1 ever made, the plucky little electric hatchback is finally back on the road after a nearly 20 year hiatus, much of that spent in a Georgia impound lot. Rebuilding this three-decade-old EV was no easy task but with a bunch of help, even some from GM itself, the EV1 is alive once again.

According to recent reports, watching V212 roll out of the garage was a moment 12 months in the making. It all started at the Georgia impound lot, where the V212 sold for $104,000, despite being sun-faded, tired, and legally abandoned. The forgotten EV1 was bought by Apple employee Billy Caruso, who owns several early EVs, and the restoration was done by Caruso, Jared Pink from The Questionable Garage, and GM. Engineers and designers from GM who worked on the EV1 back in the day helped support the project and offered up parts from an old donor car.

It has been revealed that caruso brought the V212 to Kettering University in Flint, Michigan, to celebrate its finished restoration, where he interviewed some of the people who worked on the original EV1 project. And the passion and love that everyone who worked on the EV1 has is evident. The EV1 wasn't the most successful car GM ever made, but it was a massively key project for the future of the brand and one that made a massive impact on everyone involved.

"Honestly, I've had a lot of really good roles in my career," said Linda Ludek Brouns, former propulsion system engineer for EV1. "Hands-down favorite was my time working on EV1.

Caruso's project wasn't an easy one. V212 received a full strip-down to bare metal, its interior was completely removed, and even its glass came out. Its interior was refreshed, it received all latest glass, and it was painted. It was a painstaking process but V212 now is about as fresh as it was in 1996.

It has been revealed that bringing cars back to life is always heartwarming for us gearheads. But when that car is as rare and special as the EV1, it's so much more meaningful. The story is made even more special by Caruso being able to show it off to the people who designed, engineered, and built it. Thankfully, due to Caruso being willing to spend six figures on a project car, The Questionable Garage's dedication to the project, and GM's help, a piece of automotive history lives on instead of wasting away in the Georgia sun.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, in bear life, as in human life, sometimes you just have to take a leap of faith. A brown bear (Ursus arctos) cub hanging around Anan Creek in Tongass National Forest in southeastern Alaska learned that this summer. Its mom, Gemini, was crossing the creek, and one cub jumped right in. But this cub? Not so sure. It stood waiting at the water’s edge, before jumping in.

For this forceful leap into the water, the park rangers have awarded Gemini’s little cub with the 2026 Yeet of Faith Award. For those keeping score at home, Gemini won this year’s helicopter mom award.

“Cubs learn at their own pace, and thanks to amazing recreation sites like Anan, we get to witness their tiny triumphs up close,” the rangers write.

Tongass National Forest’s rangers are awarding the Anan Bear Awards to the 39 bears spotted at the Anan Wildlife Observatory in Alaska over the summer.

In a recent development, tongass is the largest national forest in the United States, and covers most of Southeast Alaska, including the state’s capital city of Juneau. The area includes Mendenhall Glacier (a popular destination for Alaskan cruises), numerous hiking trails, eagles soaring above, and plenty of bears on the hunt for food. One of the hotspots for wildlife is Anan Creek, home to one of the largest runs of pink salmon in Southeast Alaska. As such, the creek is a very popular dinner spot among black and brown bears.

Industry observers note that according to Friends of Anan, 39 bears are known to feast on the salmon at Anan Creek. The population includes 31 black bears (Ursus americanus) and eight brown bears like Gemini and her cubs. Similar to their chubby counterparts farther to the north in Katmai National Park, the bears return each summer to gorge on salmon ahead of the long winter, and teach their cubs how to fish in order to survive. And also like the fat bears of Katmai, every bear around Anan Creek has their own habits and quirks.

The U.S. Forest Service tracks and documents every bear spotted at Anan, while explore.org’s cameras broadcast live streams of their behaviors.

Industry News: Amflow rolls out its first city e-bikes, packing huge torque and serious smart tech

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1079 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Amflow has made a name for itself in the electric mountain bike world with its high-performance Avinox-powered machines, but now the company is bringing that same technology to a decidedly more urban environment.
  • And while these might look like fairly conventional step-through city bikes at first glance, there’s some seriously impressive technology hiding beneath those clean lines.
  • The new Amflow UE series comes in two versions, the UE Carbon and the higher-end UE Carbon Pro, both built around a full-carbon fiber frame weighing just 2.35 kg (5.2 lb).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Amflow has made a name for itself in the electric mountain bike world with its high-performance Avinox-powered machines, but now the company is bringing that same technology to a decidedly more urban environment. The newly unveiled Amflow UE Carbon series marks the brand’s first move into the commuter e-bike market, combining a lightweight carbon fiber frame, powerful mid-drive motor, and a surprisingly long list of smart features designed for everyday riding.

And while these might look like fairly conventional step-through city bikes at first glance, there’s some seriously impressive technology hiding beneath those clean lines.

The new Amflow UE series comes in two versions, the UE Carbon and the higher-end UE Carbon Pro, both built around a full-carbon fiber frame weighing just 2.35 kg (5.2 lb).

The complete bike weighs as little as 20.9 kg (46 lb), which is fairly impressive considering the amount of hardware Amflow has packed into it, including front suspension, a suspension dropper seatpost, integrated lighting, and cargo racks.

Both models use the Avinox M2 mid-drive motor, which delivers up to 125 Nm of torque. That’s an enormous amount of torque for a city bike, and should make short work of steep hills, especially when carrying groceries or other cargo. And to put things into perspective, a lot of city e-bikes have barely 60 Nm for torque, so Amflow is knocking it out of the park for urban power.

A removable 600 Wh battery provides a claimed maximum range of 132 km (82 miles) in the lowest power assist mode, while fast charging can refill the battery in just 2 hours and 23 minutes.

The bikes also feature Avinox’s intelligent traction control system and a upcoming Auto Boost function that automatically provides additional assistance when the system detects demanding conditions, such as accelerating from a stop or climbing a steep hill.

In other words, riders get much of the sophisticated motor technology developed for high-performance electric mountain bikes, but in a package designed for commuting to work or picking up groceries.

Industry observers note that the bike is listed as weighing 20.9 kg (46 lb), though that figure conveniently excludes the front and rear racks, mudguards, pedals, kickstand, bike lock, bottle cage, and chainguard. So figure a few extra pounds for all of that gear, and you’re in the right ballpark.

The main difference between the two models is their drivetrain.

The higher-end UE Carbon Pro ($3,899) uses a customized three-speed electronically shifted internally geared hub paired with a Gates carbon belt drive. That should make it particularly appealing to commuters who want a quiet, clean, low-maintenance setup without worrying about chain lubrication or derailleur adjustments.

The more affordable UE Carbon ($3,499) instead uses a 10-speed electronic derailleur developed with TRP.

Both models support automatic shifting, allowing the bike to handle gear changes without requiring the rider to constantly think about them.

Amflow has also gone fairly wild with the technology integration.

There’s a 1.4-inch touchscreen display mounted on the handlebars, a wireless phone charging mount offering 15W wireless charging or 20W USB-C charging, and integrated lighting with automatic low-light activation and brake-sensing functionality.

The bikes even include a hardened steel frame lock on the rear wheel, Apple Find My integration, and a Lost Mode feature that can lock down certain components if the bike is stolen.

Apple Watch connectivity allows riders to check their bike’s status and unlock it, while heart-rate-based assistance can automatically adjust motor output to help riders maintain a target heart rate zone.

Some of these features, like the security and tracking, are immediately effective for nearly all riders, while other high-tech features like the heart rate-based pedal assist can provide even more functionality for niche riders looking to bridge the gap between riding for transportation and riding for fitness.

Of course, all the fancy technology in the world doesn’t mean much if a commuter bike can’t handle everyday errands.

Fortunately, Amflow appears to have taken the practical side seriously.

The bikes feature a low step-through frame, upright riding position, 65 mm suspension fork, and a suspension dropper seatpost offering 125 mm of height adjustment and approximately 30 mm of suspension travel.

The 26×2.0-inch Maxxis tires should also provide a comfortable ride over less-than-perfect city streets.

There’s a front rack rated for 20 kg (44 lb) and a rear rack rated for 27 kg (59.5 lb), with the latter supporting the MIK HD mounting system for compatible accessories, including child seats.

The standard frame is designed to accommodate riders from 155 to 190 cm (5’1” to 6’3”), while a smaller version for riders down to 140 cm (4’7”) is expected in 2027.

I’ve been impressed with the technology coming out of the Avinox ecosystem, and it’s exciting to see that technology finally make its way into a more practical city-focused electric bicycle.

As much as I love high-performance electric mountain bikes, the reality is that most people aren’t spending their mornings bombing down mountain trails. They’re commuting to work, dropping kids off at school, and running errands.

And that’s where electric bicycles can make an even bigger difference.

The Amflow UE series seems to take a refreshingly comprehensive approach to urban riding. The powerful motor is nice, but I’m arguably more interested in the belt drive, integrated security, cargo capacity, automatic shifting, and built-in phone charging.

Sources indicate that those are the kinds of features that can make an electric bicycle genuinely easier to live with every day. And as someone who actually commutes with an e-bike each day as my main form of transportation, these bikes are really speaking to me!

If you ask me, it’s great to see another high-performance e-bike manufacturer recognizing that the future of electric bicycles isn’t just about riding farther and faster on trails. It’s also about making everyday transportation better for the less exciting type of riding, too.

Machina Aims to Democratize Car Customization with Innovative Robots

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that automotive manufacturing is a laborious, resource-intensive process.
  • It has been revealed that machina’s business is based around its RoboCraftsman platform, which it basically pitches as a factory in a box.
  • Machina Labs was founded in 2019 and so far has mostly served clients in the aerospace and defense industries.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that automotive manufacturing is a laborious, resource-intensive process. While the complex metropolises that are modern car factories work well for high-volume products, it is often prohibitively expensive for automakers to retool these plants to create distinct body panels for limited-production models. Now a California-based company called Machina Labs aims to plug that gap with an innovative metal manufacturing process that promises speed, flexibility, and cost-savings.

See all results for used cars for sale near 29445.

It has been revealed that machina’s business is based around its RoboCraftsman platform, which it basically pitches as a factory in a box. The system uses a pair of large robotic arms to perform a variety of tasks on metal panels, from striking designs into pre-stamped panels to fully forming new pieces. The robotic arms are controlled by software that can switch between different projects as quickly as Machina can upload new designs, and the system also scans the completed panel to see if any additional work needs to be done, and to trim, finish, and heat treat the pieces. The entire setup can be folded into two shipping containers that can then be easily transported.

Machina Labs was founded in 2019 and so far has mostly served clients in the aerospace and defense industries. But now Machina wants to enter the automotive space, launching a newly introduced division called Machina Rebellis. With its RoboCraftsman platform, Machina aims to give automakers a way to skip the costly retooling process, with its technology providing a more efficient method to promptly craft customizable body panels, allowing OEMs to efficiently build more distinctive limited-edition cars.

Machina’s interest in the automotive world started a few years back when it built a truck called the Anvil, based on the Ford F-150 Lightning, to demonstrate the unique body panels its metalworking machines could produce. While still fairly crude, this early prototype got Toyota’s attention, and the Japanese automotive giant is now an investor in Machina Labs via Woven Capital, Toyota’s venture capital division.

Industry observers note that the process has improved vastly since the Anvil was built, and to demonstrate this, Machina Labs created a newly introduced show vehicle, the Lassen, which is being shown at the Los Angeles auto show. Based on a Toyota Tacoma, the Lassen wears a unique hood, tailgate, and fenders, showing off the sort of customization that Machina’s process is capable of. Machina worked with Callum, the design house formed by Ian Callum, to pen the look of these panels before manufacturing them using the RoboCraftsman platform.

See all results for used cars for sale near 29445.

According to recent reports, while the Lassen isn’t a drastic departure from a standard Tacoma, the changes that Machina made would typically take around four to six months to produce via traditional methods, the organization mentioned at a media event at its second factory in Chatsworth, California. Using its RoboCraftsman platform, Machina was able to take the Lassen from sketches to a finished product in just two and a half weeks.

It has been revealed that the Lassen highlights off Machina’s two main capabilities. The hood and tailgate demonstrate the RoboCraftsman’s ability to re-strike pre-stamped panels with custom designs. The Lassen’s tailgate has a bold embossed Machina script, while the hood also states Machina and has a topographical map of its namesake, Mount Lassen in California. The RoboCraftsman platform can put just about any design on a metal panel, and Machina also had tailgates on display featuring a retro Toyota design and a Los Angeles Rams logo.

The fenders, meanwhile, are entirely fresh panels formed by the RoboCraftsman, and they have a bulging, powerful look. These fenders started as a sheet of metal—Machina works in both aluminum and steel—before being shaped by the robotic arms. This process is a bit slower than the re-striking process, which can take minutes to complete, but a fully formed panel can be finished within hours.

It has been revealed that machina believes its RoboCraftsman platform is best suited to production runs in the hundreds and thousands. This could include special-edition models for large OEMs, or working with aftermarket companies to create body kits and other visual customizations. OEMs can also use Machina’s process to promptly create body panels for early pre-production vehicles, typically an expensive and time-consuming part of the development cycle. In the future, Machina also envisions sending its RoboCraftsman units directly to OEM manufacturing sites to speed up the process even further.

It has been revealed that over the past decade, high-end carmakers realized there is a lot of money in personalization, leading to a surge of one-off and limited-production supercars, designed to the exacting specification desired by their wealthy buyers. These cars, often hand-built, are incredibly expensive. Machina Labs indicates that its RoboCraftsman platform could democratize customization, with the speed and flexibility at which it can work allowing automakers to save money and offer personalized details on more ordinary, everyday vehicles.

The RoboCraftsman platform provides a way to swiftly manufacture custom body panels, and the flexibility to switch among a large number of different projects in a short amount of time. The Lassen serves as a proof of concept as Machina courts automotive companies, and seeing the RoboCraftsman operate in person, we certainly see a space in the automotive world for Machina’s quick and flexible manufacturing innovation.

Nearly 3 million pages of military records from the War of 1812 are finally online

💡 Key Takeaways
  • After 16 years of painstaking work, the National Archives and its collaborators have finally completed digitizing over 90,000 pension applications submitted to the United States government following the War of 1812.
  • While archivists previously digitized a similar collection related to the American Revolutionary War, the newly introduced documents will help fill in knowledge gaps between early 19th century military events and the 1850 federal census.
  • “In the specific case of the War of 1812 pension records, there is an added priority due to their frail state where not acting may mean sacrificing these for future generations,” Oxley remarked in a recent announcement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After 16 years of painstaking work, the National Archives and its collaborators have finally completed digitizing over 90,000 pension applications submitted to the United States government following the War of 1812. The project is more than just preservation for preservation’s sake. The roughly 2.8 million pages contain long-forgotten and missing details about 19th century Americans, their families, and their everyday lives.

While archivists previously digitized a similar collection related to the American Revolutionary War, the newly introduced documents will help fill in knowledge gaps between early 19th century military events and the 1850 federal census. Patricia Oxley, president of the Federation of Genealogical Societies (FGS), explained the project was also incredibly time-sensitive.

“In the specific case of the War of 1812 pension records, there is an added priority due to their frail state where not acting may mean sacrificing these for future generations,” Oxley remarked in a recent announcement.

It has been revealed that the somewhat latest United States of America declared war on the United Kingdom on June 18, 1812, citing objections to trade restrictions with France amid the Napoleonic Wars, as well as the Royal Navy’s impressment of American sailors. Although the conflict famously included a British attack on Washington D.C. that resulted in the burning of the White House and U.S. Capitol, little shifted geopolitically between the two nations following the ratification of the Treaty of Ghent on February 17, 1815. The U.S. tallied around 15,000 casualties, while the U.K. and Canada saw about 10,700 deaths. Another 9,000 Indigenous fighters died while enlisted between the two sides.

Recent findings suggest that today’s military records are meticulously documented and stored digitally, but applying for benefits such as pensions was a much more labor-intensive process during the 19th century. With the burden of proof on each applicant, veterans were required to supply lengthy accounts of their service. Each War of 1812 pension file is liable to contain not just combat information, but the names and personal details of fellow soldiers, family members, spouses, and countless other relations.

“Our consumers have been asking for the War of 1812 pension records for some time, and I expect this collection to be very popular based on the rich war time detail it contains,” added Brian Hansen, general manager at Fold3, Ancestry’s military records service and National Archives collaborator.

Recent findings suggest that the collection also includes a full-text search feature using handwriting recognition technology. This lets owners explore the files based on every named individual, and not simply the primary veteran applicants. The pension records are presently available for free on Fold3’s website, and are being added to the National Archives catalog on a rolling basis.

In a recent development, correction 11/20/26 9:30 a.m. EST: A previous version of this article incorrectly stated the pension archive contained around 7 million files. This was based on an initial assessment from researchers in 2010. The article has been updated to reflect the more accurate tally.

This memory-hunting adventure is told from the perspective of Firefly, which will also explain how she entered the dreamscape initially and met the squad.

The new playable character is The Dahlia, whose power is linked to the the Remembrance path, which allows her to fabricate memories. Despite taking her powers from the Remembrance, The Dhalia actually follows the Path of Nihility in-game: she’s a 5-Star character who shines in teams dealing Break DMG.

The Dhalia can unleash a Gloomy Zone that causes Toughness Reduction inflicted by allies to trigger Super Break DMG, even before you break your enemies’ Weaknesses. The Dahlia can also invite one teammate to become her Dance Partner, which allows them (and her) to deal additional Super Break DMG each time they attack an enemy. If you trigger her Ultimate after picking a Dance Partner, she applies Type Weaknesses of both partners to enemies.

While The Dahlia is the only upcoming character appearing in this final Amphoreus update, there'll be reruns aplenty, with an unusual third banner phase to make up for the extra long wait for 4.0. Appropriately for her role in the story, Firefly will make her return alongside The Dahlia in Phase 1, while Fugue and Lingsha will both have banner reruns in Phase 2, which is expected on January 7th. A bonus two-week-long Phase 3 will then begin on January 28th, seeing brief reappearances for popular returning characters Aglaea and Sunday, before things (presumably) go back to normal with the new annual update.

Recent findings suggest that something else to look forward to in 3.8 is The Chrysos Awoo Championship, which invites players to become chimera trainers and compete in team-based battles. The Remnants of Twilight event kicks off with the new patch, too, featuring its own set of challenges. However, HoYoverse have confirmed that there won't be an extra event during Phase 3 — but hopefully that'll give you some time to wrap up the last of the Amphoreus story content, which is longer than the previous four chapters put together.

#17698. Industry News: Ford Just Started Fathom LFP Battery Production In Michigan. It's A Substantial Deal

Industry News: Ford Just Started Fathom LFP Battery Production In Michigan. It's A Substantial Deal

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (778 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Insideevs

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ford just reached a critical milestone in the development of its Fathom electric truck.
  • Sources indicate that one can’t overstate how key the Marshall plant is for Ford.
  • According to recent reports, it has an annual production capacity of 20 gigawatt-hours and can manufacture 50 battery packs every hour.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ford just reached a critical milestone in the development of its Fathom electric truck. The firm has started manufacturing low-cost lithium-iron-phosphate (LFP) battery packs at its $3 billion BlueOval Battery Park Michigan, located a couple hours west of Detroit, in Marshall, MI. These are production-grade LFP batteries which will first be used in Fathom prototypes before full-scale manufacturing begins next year.

Sources indicate that one can’t overstate how key the Marshall plant is for Ford. It’s the first plant in the U.S. to manufacture LFP batteries for mainstream consumer vehicle use domestically. LG Energy Solution also produces LFP batteries in the U.S.—supplying to GM and Tesla—but they’re dedicated to stationary energy storage systems. Ford’s 2 million-square-foot facility is dedicated to automotive LFP batteries.

According to recent reports, it has an annual production capacity of 20 gigawatt-hours and can manufacture 50 battery packs every hour. It’s a vertically integrated plant, where materials like raw lithium and iron-phosphate powder go in one end, and fully assembled, ready-to-install battery packs come out the other. All anode and cathode production, as well as major production processes in between, happen inside the plant.

It has been revealed that alan Clarke, the vice president of advanced development projects at Ford, remarked the company is moving fast to bring the Fathom to the market. In a relatively short time period, he claimed, Ford had developed the all-upcoming Universal EV Platform that will underpin its future EVs, an all-new production system at the Louisville Assembly Plant, and domestic LFP battery production.

“Not having a team that existed to have a battery factory, a unicasting factory, an entirely new most automated vehicle production facility that Ford's ever produced in less than five years would be I think faster than China speed,” Clarke said during a media roundtable at the BlueOval Battery Park Michigan on Tuesday.

Clarke previously worked at Tesla for 12 years, helping create the Model S, followed by development work for the Model X, Model Y, Model 3, and Cybertruck.

BlueOval Battery Park Michigan drone photo.

I toured Ford’s LFP plant this week, and I think it’s one of the most advanced, highly-automated battery facilities in the U.S. Michigan, America’s automotive manufacturing hub for a century, certainly hasn’t seen anything like it in its history.

According to recent reports, part of the reason why the facility is so cutting-edge comes from Ford’s LFP licensing deal with China’s CATL, the world’s largest and the most advanced battery maker. The U.S. has been lagging behind China and Europe in the battery technology race. Ford is now bringing that technical know-how back to the U.S. even if that means licensing technology from CATL.

More importantly, Ford officials said the upcoming plant is fully compliant with the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) rules. Raw materials used to make batteries here do not come from what the U.S. government designates as Foreign Entities of Concern (FEOC). Even though the technology is from CATL, the critical materials aren’t sourced from U.S. FEOCs such as China, Russia and North Korea. (China controls the vast majority of the global critical materials supply chain.).

Final inspection of the Ford Fathom's LFP prismatic cells.

It has been revealed that the plant is fully owned and operated by Ford, but CATL engineers helped the organization set up thousands of incredibly complex production tools. They’re also helping train workers to operate high-tech equipment and install tight quality control systems to help Ford deliver the affordable EV that it has long promised. The prismatic LFP cell itself is unique to Ford and not something that exists in CATL’s global portfolio.

Meng Wang, the director and chief engineer of battery cell industrialization at Ford summed up the CATL partnership well. “To shorten our time to market, we decided to learn from the best,” Wang said. “Throughout the process, CATL passed on critical knowledge to Ford, including the equipment functions, manufacturing process, and also quality controls.”.

Preorders for the Ford Fathom will begin early 2027 and production and deliveries are expected to begin by the end of next year.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This article is part of a mental health content series called “Mind Games,” in which Healthline editor Morgan Mandriota draws on personal experience and research to challenge misconceptions, reduce stigma, review trends, and share hot takes and lessons learned about what it means to be mentally well.

Coffee and I don’t exactly have the best relationship.

My morning cup tends to give me jitters, worsen my anxiety, and keep me up until 2 a.m. if I drink it past noon. As an already anxious human, the last thing I need is to exacerbate my symptoms, even if it’s coming from a delicious source.

Over a year ago, I noticed that my anxiety was higher than usual. I was also tossing and turning and waking up at all hours of the night for weeks on end.

One night in particular, I woke up every hour for 8 hours. Naturally, I wanted to blame it on the full moon or anything other than my beloved coffee, but alas, I realized that my caffeine consumption was the most likely culprit.

It has been revealed that could I have aimed to set a strict drinking schedule to see if that fixed things? Sure. But instead, I decided to quit cold turkey and undergo an experiment to see how I’d feel going coffee-free for the first time in years.

Industry observers note that over the next 8 months, I’d swap my coffee station for a matcha setup, dabble in exotic herbal blends from my local teahouse, and become a self-proclaimed tea connoisseur. Lo and behold, my anxiety eased up, and my sleep quality improved, too.

Fast forward to 4 months ago, when I hopped back on the coffee train. But this time, I’m relying on a handy amino acid to help avoid anxiety and other unwanted side effects: L-theanine.

Health and wellness touch everyone’s life differently. This is one person’s story. The views and opinions expressed are those of the speaker and do not necessarily reflect the views or positions of Healthline Media and should not serve as a substitute for medical advice from a healthcare professional.

L-theanine is mainly found in green and black tea and one type of wild mushroom. The mental health benefits of L-theanine consumption are an emerging area of research, but one 2024 review found that consuming around 200 to 400 milligrams (mg) may help relieve symptoms in people with anxiety disorders.

According to recent reports, still, anecdotal reports suggest there may be benefits of adding L-theanine to coffee. Over the last 5 years, the combo has been gaining traction on Reddit and TikTok for managing caffeine-related side effects.

Despite an overwhelming amount of rave reviews online, I couldn’t find much research to support these claims, so I spoke with a neurologist to see if they had any thoughts.

“This trend has real science behind it,” stated Fawad Mian, MD, who is board certified in neurology, clinical neurophysiology, and sleep medicine and the founder of Ascend Regenerative.

“Controlled studies show caffeine plus L-theanine improves focus and attention more than caffeine alone, and some suggest it softens caffeine’s side effects, like tiredness, headaches, and blood pressure spikes,” Mian mentioned. “It smooths caffeine’s effects but doesn’t erase them, so it’s not a license to drink more coffee,” he added.

With all of this in mind, especially after realizing just how calm I was while drinking black and green teas during my coffee break, I decided to give it a try.

After about 4 months of “testing,” I’ve found that adding L-theanine to my coffee works extremely well for me.

No more anxiety, scatterbrain, shakiness, or staying up until 3 a.m. And no lifestyle overhaul needed. The supplement, which I prefer in liquid form, has become a seamless addition to my daily routine.

Every morning, I make a fresh batch of French press coffee with (strong) local beans, then I squeeze some L-theanine into my cup.

I’ve noticed that I get the usual coffee benefits like improved focus and concentration, plus a nice, calm, stable energy throughout the day.

According to recent reports, even if I drink it until 2 p.m., I’m fighting to keep my eyes open at night before I finally fall asleep around 10. Perhaps this is because L-theanine may also support quality sleep.

Mindful L-Theanine Drops is the liquid supplement that I use every day.

In a recent development, I add a one-second squeeze (which contains 200 mg of L-theanine) into my morning coffee, then I’m good to go. I even started carrying a bottle in my bag just in case I get a latte from a coffee shop on a whim.

It has been revealed that you can also add it to a glass of water, a cup of tea, or another drink of your choosing. It’s unflavored, so it doesn’t alter the taste of your drinks. Real secret stuff.

Out of curiosity, and because I’m a natural skeptic and overthinker, I asked Mian if my positive experience could be a placebo effect, or if I’m seeing real results.

It has been revealed that “Expectation may play a small role, but the effect is biologically plausible,” he said. “L-theanine boosts calming brain activity that offsets caffeine’s stimulation, and 200 mg matches the doses used in studies.” However, he noted that it doesn’t speed caffeine clearance, so drinking coffee only in the morning still matters for sleep quality.

While L-theanine is generally safe to consume, it’s best to speak with a healthcare professional first, especially if you’re pregnant, nursing, receiving cancer treatment, or taking blood pressure medication or sedatives.

“Choose a third-party tested brand, and if caffeine makes you anxious, cutting back is still the simplest fix,” Mian added.

Recent findings suggest that so, if you’re anything like me and drinking coffee also leads to anxiety and jitters for you, I highly recommend trying this supplement once you get the green light from your doctor. It’s been working for me. It may work well for you, too.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, ford has entered the battery business. The first LFP battery cells are now rolling off the assembly line at Ford’s BlueOval Battery Park plant in Michigan and are headed to power Fathom prototypes in Kentucky.

In a recent development, how do you get more out of a battery without adding weight or more cells? According to Alan Clarke, Ford’s vice president of advanced development projects, who is also leading its Universal Electric Vehicle (UEV) platform, the answer lies in lithium iron phosphate (LFP) technology.

Unlike traditional lithium-ion, LFP batteries use no nickel or cobalt, which helps reduce costs. They also typically hold up better after years of use and charging.

Sources indicate that to make it a reality, Ford turned to CATL, the leading global EV battery manufacturer. Ford uses CATL’s licensed technology and manufacturing expertise at its BlueOval Battery Park Michigan plant.

Ford stated it will be the first in the US to deliver LFP batteries for mainstream automotive use, with the battery cells now rolling off the line in Michigan.

The first LFP battery cells are headed to Ford’s Louisville Assembly Plant and will be used to power Fathom prototypes, its first vehicle based on the UEV platform.

Sources indicate that ford designed and engineered the Fathom from the ground up for efficiency. As such, it chose prismatic battery cells because they fit directly into the chassis, reducing structural costs.

With cells now being delivered from a plant that it owns and operates, Ford noted it will use the knowledge gained in Michigan to support more affordable EVs and Ford Energy, its fresh battery energy storage business in Kentucky.

At Ford’s fresh battery plant in Michigan, assembly lines can deliver 40 cells every minute, making it one of the fastest LFP prismatic battery assembly lines outside China.

Although the accelerated output drives down costs, Ford noted employees use AI-powered image recognition and inspection tools to spot defects in real time and maintain quality.

“Our goal is to make defective cells so rare that we track their frequency per billion cells rather than per million,” Ford stated.

With production testing now underway, Ford prepares to have the battery pack plant in Michigan up and running in 2027, ahead of schedule.

Ford will open preorders for the Fathom in early 2027, starting at $28,350 for the standard-range model.

CEO Jim Farley noted on the tech giant’s third-quarter earnings call last month that the Fathom, Ford’s first vehicle based on the UEV platform, remains on track to launch in Q4 2027.

Farley said the Fathom is a “breakthrough product” that’s highly capable and still affordable. The starting MSRP is under $30,000, and the low cost of ownership is perfect for today’s market, he added.

Ford and Slate both producing vehicles with US-produced LFP batteries is a great milestone. Hopefully we can keep pushing our domestic battery supply chain forward.

Ford said the Fathom will offer more interior space than a Toyota RAV4, and it will cost less to own over five years than a three-year-old used Tesla Model Y.

It has been revealed that the pickup will be the first vehicle to integrate Apple Maps directly into the navigation system. All versions will be BlueCruise-capable for hands-free driving, with standard Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, plus bidirectional charging capabilities.

Although we have yet to see it, Ford said the Fathom features a “large touchscreen display” with easy-to-use navigation.

Ford has not revealed battery specs or range, but we do know the pickup will have an NACS port after several prototypes were spotted at a Tesla Supercharger over the summer.

According to recent reports, turn off reality TV and turn on the bald eagle cams. It’s all the drama you need.

In a recent development, when internet-famous bald eagle Shadow seemingly welcomed a mysterious new female into his nest earlier this week, many fans have questioned the whereabouts of Kaydee. After the death of Shadow’s longtime partner Jackie in August, he had been spotted spending time with the 4-year-old banded female eagle named KD1 (later renamed Kaydee). It seemed like the eagles might head into mating season as a pair, but after the arrival of a new, large female, it’s unclear how the relationships will all shake out.

Sources indicate that since the appearance of the mystery female, nicknamed Significant Beautiful Visitor or BBV by some fans, Kaydee has disappeared from view of Friends of Big Bear Valley (FOBBV)’s two cameras. She was last spotted by the cameras on November 14 in the Roost Tree, according to FOBBV. Despite concerns that she may be injured or had left the area, wildlife photographers have continued to document Kaydee’s presence near Big Bear Lake as recently as November 18.

Photographer Alla Shumko shared photos of Kaydee perched near Big Bear Lake on November 18. Kaydee’s double bands are visible as she observed a scuffle between younger eagles fighting over fish.

Mating season is well underway, so viewers of FOBBV’s 24/7 livecams have been watching closely for signs that Shadow has selected a fresh partner. Shadow has worked with both Kaydee and the new eagle on nest maintenance and shared “beaky kisses” with each female, both signs of bonding in bald eagles. Bald eagle mating involves a bit of aerial acrobatics—copulating pairs can be seen in what’s called a “cartwheel display,” in which they lock talons in mid-air while tumbling down to the ground. Male eagles do not have an external phallus, so mating occurs via a touch of cloacas. Vocalizations can typically be heard during the act, which lasts about 7 to 12 seconds, according to Raptor Resource.

As this is nature, we humans can’t predict or influence who Shadow will pick as a new partner. Or if he picks at all. All we can do is watch and wait and let nature take its course.

Breaking: West Coast Customs turns a Tesla Model 3 into a 1955 Chevy Bel Air

💡 Key Takeaways
  • West Coast Customs has finished its first electric Chevy Bel Air, and there’s not much Chevy left under the paint.
  • The result, called Project B-Zero, looks like a ’55 Chevy from the curb and like a Model 3 as soon as you open the door.
  • In the shop’s new video, “The First Ever Electric Bel Air,” founder and CEO Ryan Friedlinghaus explains that a longtime client, Troy Swope, wants to convert an entire car collection to electric and picked the Bel Air to go first.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Coast Customs has finished its first electric Chevy Bel Air, and there’s not much Chevy left under the paint. The Burbank shop cut the body off a Tesla Model 3, kept the entire rolling platform, and set a 1955 Bel Air shell on top of it.

The result, called Project B-Zero, looks like a ’55 Chevy from the curb and like a Model 3 as soon as you open the door. And it charges at Tesla Superchargers.

In the shop’s new video, “The First Ever Electric Bel Air,” founder and CEO Ryan Friedlinghaus explains that a longtime client, Troy Swope, wants to convert an entire car collection to electric and picked the Bel Air to go first. WCC had previously built the same client a Chevelle with a big gas engine.

Industry observers note that friedlinghaus, who drives a Tesla himself, decided against pulling the Model 3’s motors and battery out and fitting them into the old Chevy. Instead, the Tesla stays whole and the Chevy becomes the body kit.

In a recent development, that’s a formula WCC has used for years with gas cars. The shop calls it “old school meets newly introduced school”: an old GTO body on a new GTO, an old Camaro on a new Camaro, an old Mustang on a new Mustang. B-Zero is the first time it did it with a Tesla underneath.

“It sounds easy, but that process was tedious,” Friedlinghaus said.

Sources indicate that before any Chevy sheet metal went on, the crew took the bare Model 3 skateboard for a spin on the streets around the shop, with no doors, no lights and no seatbelts. Friedlinghaus joked about how many safety violations they were racking up. But it drove fine.

Recent findings suggest that the real headache was the wheelbase. A 1955 Chevy rides on a 115-inch wheelbase, while the Model 3 sits at 113.2 inches. On its gas builds, WCC can cut, shorten or lengthen the newer car’s frame to match the old body. You can’t do that with a Tesla, since the floor is the battery pack.

So the shop changed the body instead, stretching the Bel Air’s rear wheel wells so the wheels sit where they look like they belong.

Sources indicate that the client wanted the exterior to read as a mostly stock Bel Air. The original car was red, so WCC kept it red, with a satin finish and gloss black accents.

Inside, it’s a Model 3. The shop kept the Tesla’s interior, including the steering wheel and center touchscreen, and modified it to fit the Chevy body. The seats got black suede with white stitching in an octagon pattern that Friedlinghaus noted was borrowed from the Lamborghini Urus, plus red accents and a “B-Zero” script on the dash.

Friedlinghaus noted the goal was for people to see “a really nice Bel Air” from the outside, then open the door and find a Tesla. He also expects some double takes when it pulls into a Supercharger station.

He admits the reaction has been split. Plenty of people are mad that the shop electrified a Bel Air, and plenty of others think it came out great. The client is clearly in the second camp, describing the car as easy to drive and saying every trip in it feels like an event.

Here’s the full build video from West Coast Customs:.

This is sick. I know Tesla doesn’t care about personal car ownership anymore, but they should really sell their platform so shops can do these conversions without using salvage vehicles.

Sources indicate that well I was really interested in this build until I read how they kept it entirely Tesla inside. Not at all what I was thinking or what I'd call a true old car conversion to EV. Instead, they simply transformed the outside of a Tesla into an old looking car. To me, even the outside looks too far removed from the original Bel Air and more like a street rod. If that's what the owner wants and paid for, great.

Industry observers note that but for me, I would never do a conversion like that. I really want to convert an older 70's or 80's or early 90's Cadillac into an EV. But for me, I will insist that the outside and inside look 100% like the original car with just an EV powertrain.

Don’t get me wrong, if you can recycle a salvage, that’s good, but it can’t always be done.

Compare it to the 1966 Mustang that a Sacramento Tesla parts shop converted earlier this year. That project took about $40,000 and two years, with the team grafting sections of a Model 3 floor into the Mustang. It’s an amazing build, but it’s a lot of custom engineering. WCC’s approach skips most of that. You keep Tesla’s crash structure, battery thermal management, software, over-the-air updates and Supercharger access, because you never took the car apart in the first place. It’s closer to what S-Klub did with its Model 3-based Mercedes 300SL than a traditional drivetrain swap.

Sources indicate that the purists will hate it. That’s fine. This Bel Air will get driven more in a year than most restored ones get driven in a decade.

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1911 w)
📖 Baca
