📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the time has arrived for another Arc Raiders patch, and Embark has certainly delivered. Today’s patch, version 1.6.0, is among the smallest the game has received so far, focusing almost exclusively on disabling map exploits.

Perhaps more key than the patch itself, however, is the announcement the developer made around it.

Starting off with patch 1.6.0, it takes out a particular zipline on Stella Montis, the game’s most recent addition ot the map roster. Some players used said zipline to get out of bounds, something the game has been battling on several of its maps.

According to recent reports, on Blue Gate, the patch fixes a collision issue that allowed players to vault through a wall, and fall to their death. The map fixes continue with another on Spaceport Launch Tower, which takes out a gap in collision that players have been able to shoot through.

In a recent development, the last change in this upgrade affects gameplay feel around Arc enemies. Certain materials in the game’s world weren’t blocking their vision - or fire - when they should have, and this has now been fixed.

Alongside today’s patch, Embark also announced that going forward, we’re going to see fewer patches for Arc Raiders. The game has been getting updates almost every Thursday since it launched in late October.

Now that most of the major problems have been fixed, the studio is shifting to a slower patching cadence. Critical fixes will still be issued as soon as they’re developed, but don’t expect a patch each week going forward.

Embark also revealed that patch releases and in-game store rotations will now occur on Tuesdays. You should also expect the next few weeks to be quiet, as members of the team go on holiday breaks.

Recent findings suggest that but, before everyone goes away, the game is going to get one more significant update. The last item on Arc Raiders’ roadmap, revealed in early November, is the Cold Snap event. This is on track for Tuesday, bringing some new content alongside a few other fixes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alpitronic, the organization that makes the DC fast chargers used by Ionna, Walmart, Mercedes-Benz, BP Pulse, and others, is building a fresh factory in the United States that will boost output of its 400- and 1,000-kilowatt stalls.

The manufacturer’s new 173,315-square-foot facility, located in Fort Mill, South Carolina, will create 70 new jobs and will also act as a testing lab, repair center, logistics hub, and warehouse.

Alpitronic, which has its North American headquarters in Charlotte, North Carolina, and its global headquarters in Bolzano, Italy, said it will invest $33.94 million in the new facility, with $200,000 coming from York County’s Coordinating Council for Economic Development in the form of a Set-Aside grant to assist with the costs of building improvements.

According to recent reports, “North America is central to our next phase of growth, and investing in our manufacturing capabilities is key to supporting that expansion,” said Patrik Herrnegger, Alpitronic Americas CEO. “Our Fort Mill facility will put U.S. production under our direct control, bringing us closer to our customers and enabling us to serve them more efficiently. We thank South Carolina and York County for their partnership as we prepare to begin production in early 2027.”.

Back in 2024, the company worked with a third-party production partner to open its first local manufacturing facility in Wisconsin. Now, manufacturing has moved in-house, with Alpitronic wholly owning the production operation.

Sources indicate that the fresh South Carolina plant will assemble HYC400 and HYC1000 stalls, Alpitronic noted. The HYC400 all-in-one dispensers can deliver up to 400 kW of power to a single connected electric vehicle without needing a separate power cabinet, and are the current charger of choice for Ionna and Walmart.

The higher-powered HYC1000 system is composed of a 1,000-kW power cabinet and up to four stalls that can deliver up to 600 kW to a single EV. Each stall can have two ports, and the system can dynamically allocate power to each vehicle to make the best use of the available power.

According to recent reports, what makes the firm's dispensers different from most competitors is the use of silicon carbide components, which lower energy losses and, subsequently, the amount of money EV drivers have to pay for a top-up. According to Alpitronic, SiC modules enable 97.5% efficiency and allow for smaller, quieter, and cooler stalls.

Alpitronic’s new factory in Fort Mill, South Carolina, is scheduled to go online in February 2027.

The magnetic chargers and power banks use the Qi2 25W wireless standard, and the storage boxes range from a two-bay starter unit to an eight-bay model.

A fold-flat Qi2 charger for a phone and earbuds.

A hotel nightstand usually has room for one charger. The UGREEN MagFlow 2-in-1 Foldable Magnetic Wireless Charger folds flat for a bag pocket, then opens into a magnetic phone stand with a second pad for wireless earbuds. It’s $28.49 in black (was $59.99), and UGREEN lists the white version at $29.99. The charger supports Qi2 25W, and UGREEN says its own testing took an iPhone 17 Pro Max to 50 percent in 30 minutes. Five ports and 160W for a crowded desk.

A liquid-cooled 10,000mAh magnetic power bank.

In a recent development, BYD is preparing to launch a new midsize SUV under its personalized, off-road-focused sub-brand. The new SUV was spotted testing, offering an early look at its boxy, rugged-looking design.

Fang Cheng Bao, or FCB as many call it, is another BYD sub-brand, alongside Denza and Yangwang.

It also sells the Tai series, designed more as everyday family vehicles, such as the Tai 7. BYD sells the Tai 7 as the Ti 7 under its own brand in Europe and the UK, where Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) has taken legal action, alleging it’s a copycat of the Defender.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, BYD is gearing up to add another SUV to the lineup. FCB’s general manager, Xiong Tianbo, previously announced that the Tai 6, or Ti 6, will launch in 2027.

Ahead of its official debut, the latest Ti 6 was captured in China. Although it’s still covered, the images sent to Autohome suggest it retains the boxy, upright design of the larger Ti 7 but appears slightly smaller.

Unlike the Ti 7’s split-headlight design, the smaller SUV features redesigned headlights. Like most of BYD’s newly introduced higher-end vehicles, the SUV is equipped with a LiDAR to support advanced safety and convenience features.

BYD has not revealed battery or powertrain specs, but the Ti 6 (Tai 6) is expected to be offered in pure electric (EV) and plug-in hybrid (PHEV) variants.

It will likely offer a similar setup to the Ti 7. The Ti 7 PHEV uses a 1.5L engine and an electric motor that delivers a combined 360 kW (482 hp).

The pure electric version with a single motor delivers 300 kW (402 hp), while the dual-motor variant delivers 515 kW (690 hp).

Since the Tai 7 (Ti 7) starts at 179,800 yuan ($27,000), the smaller Tai 6 (Ti 6) will likely be priced in the 150,00 yuan ($22,500) range.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, zenless Zone Zero brought some hot fresh information and a first look at its next major faction as part of The Game Awards 2025 ceremony. As part of the showcase, we got a glimpse of Ye Shunguang and Zhao - two upcoming Agents.

The segment also teased the newly introduced Angels of Delusion faction, though details on that are slim.

The gameplay reveal for Ye Shunguang and Zhao was very much the highlight of what was ultimately a smaller segment. Ye Shunguang is Zenless Zone Zero’s first dual-form Agent. She’s a Void Hunter who hails from Yunkui Summit.

Shunguang is a master swordswoman, and she can shift between two different forms. Her combat looks smooth and stylish, with a lot of aerial attacks and fast sword play. Zhao should be familiar to anyone who plays ZZZ. The rabbit Thiren has a bit of a slippery playstyle, swiftly weaving across the battlefield to deliver attacks with her greataxe.

According to recent reports, before the trailer ends, we get the Angels of Delusion teaser, which didn’t offer much, but it’s certainly something for us to look forward to in the new year. In case you missed it, Zenless Zone Zero’s latest update - Version 2.4 - is live, having arrived over two weeks ago.

As ever, make sure to check out our updated Zenless Zone Zero codes if you initiative to jump in over the next few weeks. At the moment, ZZZ V2.4 is expected to run on a slightly truncated five-week schedule, with Version 2.5 now anticipated on December 30.

Rivian’s Also Spinoff Pauses Deliveries Of Its $3,500 E-Bike After Months Of Delays

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Also, the electric mobility startup spun off from Rivian, is facing another logistics headache.
  • In an email sent to reservation holders, the organization apologized for the delay, saying it has identified a few software-based issues that are impacting some bikes, and that it wants to address the issues before resuming shipments, as first reported by The Verge.
  • In a recent development, this is the latest setback for the mobility spinoff that made headlines last year with its software-heavy bicycles and four-wheeled quads.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Also, the electric mobility startup spun off from Rivian, is facing another logistics headache. After delaying deliveries of its futuristic TM-B e-bike, the startup has paused shipments entirely to address some software problems that may lead to problematic charging behavior and phantom battery drain.

In an email sent to reservation holders, the organization apologized for the delay, saying it has identified a few software-based issues that are impacting some bikes, and that it wants to address the issues before resuming shipments, as first reported by The Verge. A firmware patch is in the works, and Also estimates that deliveries will resume in approximately two weeks, with another update scheduled for November 24.

In a recent development, this is the latest setback for the mobility spinoff that made headlines last year with its software-heavy bicycles and four-wheeled quads. The TM-B e-bike was originally scheduled to be shipped in the spring of this year, but customers started receiving their orders months later, leading to a barrage of negative comments on the Also subreddit. This prompted Saul Leiken, the startup’s product manager, to post a 661-word apology letter, in which he attributed the setbacks to strict quality standards and “significant supply chain challenges.”.

Recent findings suggest that an Also e-bike customer who received his e-bike posted a YouTube video showing how the TM-B behaves when the state of charge gets low, and how the battery drains while the bike is not in use. Aaron Draczyski stated he charged his bike in the garage up to 70%, but the state of charge went down to 30% in 24 hours without any usage. What’s more, when the battery level became critically low, the bike refused to charge, throwing an error message that claimed the battery was not installed, even though it hadn’t been removed.

It has been revealed that the Also TM-B is unlike most e-bikes out there. Designed from the ground up as a futuristic mobility vehicle, its pedals are not physically connected to the rear wheels. Instead, the rider spins a generator, which provides power to the battery and the electric motor that turns the rear wheel via a rubber belt.

The battery can be recharged via a USB-C port, there’s a round touchscreen to control all of the bike’s features, and the rider can also use a smartphone app to keep tabs on the bike remotely.

Sources indicate that the base Also TM-B starts at $3,500, but the Launch Edition models, which have yet to be shipped, cost $4,500. Earlier this year, when the startup revealed the first delays, it threw in one of its Alpha Wave helmets and a $250 credit to spend on accessories.
